statement: From the point of view of bounded reverse mathematics, the area that tries to pinpoint the minimal reasoning power needed to prove mathematical theorems, it is very interesting to understand what is the complexity of reasoning required to prove properties of expander graphs, and thus what is the complexity of reasoning in expander-based proofs such as the known proofs of SL = L [37, 39]. This paper makes a step in this direction by showing that an expander construction can be formalized within the system VNC1 . A number of open questions remain. Can we formalize expanders in a weaker theory than VNC1 , e.g., the system of TC0 reasoning? Can Reingold’s result that undirected graph connectivity is in deterministic logspace [37] be formalized in the system of logspace reasoning? The analysis of graph powering given in this paper and the analysis of replacement product given in [4] are not strong enough to achieve that goal.
